contradictions_with_stored_summary: None material; the stored summary's description matches. Archive filename 'masri2025-matcha-heavy-metal.pdf' is a misleading name but the PDF content is this Nutrients 2025 Prop 65 survey.
unresolved: Prop 65 chocolate consent-judgment values are second-hand (authors' description of ref 73); the instrument, cocoa-content tiers and Cd unit are not specified in the primary text.
disposition_reason: Online dietary survey (N = 186 Southern California adults and adolescents) that measured no metal concentrations; it reports intake of 'Chocolate Foods' (mean 9.6 g/day all participants; 12.2 g/day among consumers) and 'Chocolate Drink Powder' (2.4 and 10.8 g/day), and cites Prop 65 consent-judgment allowances for chocolate (0.225 ppm Pb, 0.960 Cd depending on cocoa content).
disposition_locator: Table 2 p.7; Results 3.2 pp.6-7; Table 3 p.9; Discussion p.17 (ref 73)

study.design: cross-sectional online 7-day food frequency survey (no contaminant measurement)
study.material_scope: consumption of chocolate foods and chocolate drink powder
study.growing_origin_vs_market: not applicable; consumers in Southern California
study.method: Qualtrics online questionnaire adapted from NHANES FFQ; powder serving masses from USDA FoodData Central
study.qa: excluded respondents with completion times <3.38 min

exposure_notes.note: 'Chocolate Foods' is a broad category not restricted to chocolate as defined on the cocoa page; regression (Table 3) shows chocolate-food intake higher among Caucasians by up to 9.2 g/day.
